title: 7-Zip: two-form password passes in Test, F3 view, Delete and Cancel not driven
problem: Feature 093 made the 7-Zip plug-in's password Unicode and kept a fallback to the old (code-page) password form: an extract runs a first pass, a retry pass for items refused under one form and a redo pass. Its probe drove the panel session through F5 only. Not driven: (1) Cancel during the test of a large item (the poll through WM_7ZIP_POLLCANCEL / ProgressAddSize(0)) and Cancel during any pass; (2) the passes in Test archive and in F3 view, and Delete from archive; (3) RAR archives under such a password. Recorded costs with it: the test decodes the cheapest encrypted item once more (up to six tests when everything is refused) with the progress bar standing still, during an update on the main thread; a damaged item under a two-form password is decoded up to three times (the first pass's partial file is deleted and written again, the keep-or-delete question as before).
evidence: specs/093-unicode-dialogs/fix-log.md, section 'S2 - the 7-Zip password', 'Not driven / open' (~lines 395-410), points 1-3. NEXT-WORK §5, B-1, bullet '7zip plugin' (L1982-1985). Functions named there: extract.h/.cpp CryptoGetTextPassword, BeginRetryPass, BeginRedoPass, EndRetryPass; 7zclient.cpp TestPassword, ChooseForm, TestArchive, Decompress. The engine is 7-Zip 26.03 with RAR/RAR5 since feature 087. Migrated from specs/NEXT-WORK.md §5 (at 7993914c).
expected: A probe drives Test archive, F3 view, Delete from archive and Cancel in each pass on a 7z archive whose password has letters outside ASCII (and on a RAR archive if one can be made); every row passes, or each defect found becomes an item of its own.
approach: Extend the 093 probe (specs/093-unicode-dialogs/probe/); Cancel can be pressed by BM_CLICK on the progress window's button on the hidden desktop. Making a RAR archive needs rar.exe (WinRAR); without it the RAR row is owed to a person.
notes: Unsure whether still open: later features (094, 113, 131 and others touching the 7-Zip plug-in) may have driven some rows - check their probes first. A 7z archive mixing the two password forms stays mixed - decided (NW §C 'Formats and old forms'), not part of this item.

title: winget: offer a per-user install (--scope user), proven in Windows Sandbox first
problem: winget install --scope user is not offered. The per-user manifest entry was part of the first submission, was blamed for the first validation failure and removed - and then the machine-only manifest failed identically, which refuted that (the real defect was the disclaimer page aborting silent installs, fixed in 0.1.7). Whether a per-user entry works has never been tested. Known: Inno Setup accepts the switches (PrivilegesRequiredOverridesAllowed=dialog implies commandline); a probe with the installer's privilege configuration took /VERYSILENT /CURRENTUSER, exited 0, installed into %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\<AppName> without elevation and wrote the HKCU uninstall key {AppId}_is1.
evidence: specs/072-winget-distribution/REMAINING-WORK.md, section P2 'Per-user installation is untested, not impossible' (procedure there) and 'Not remaining' (the publish.ps1 assertion). tools/winget/templates/installer.yaml.in line ~13 comments on the removed 'Scope: user' entry; the machine entry is at ~line 57. NEXT-WORK §6, P2 (L2040). Migrated from specs/NEXT-WORK.md §6 (at 7993914c).
expected: Either the manifest offers a user-scope installer entry that passed Tools\SandboxTest.ps1 of a winget-pkgs clone and is submitted as a pull request of its own, or the attempt failed in the sandbox and nothing reached the catalogue (the branch dropped, the reason recorded).
approach: On a branch: add to tools/winget/templates/installer.yaml.in an x64 entry with 'Scope: user', the same InstallerUrl, InstallerSha256 {{SHA256}} and InstallerSwitches Custom: /CURRENTUSER (and Custom: /ALLUSERS on the machine entry if both are wanted); reinstate the PrivilegesRequiredOverridesAllowed assertion in publish.ps1 with it; run publish.ps1 -Version <current released version> (generates and validates against the published asset, no new release needed); run Tools\SandboxTest.ps1 against that directory. Windows Sandbox must be enabled (admin; not available on GitHub runners) - that run may need a person.
notes: Do NOT change tools/winget/templates/ on main while microsoft/winget-pkgs#426090 is open: the workflow submits on release publication, and a second unreviewed change during moderation is how the first attempt went wrong. The same entry is RW072 P2 and is listed in NW §B 'Release and catalogue housekeeping' - deduplicate with those parts on import.

title: checkver plug-in still checks Open Salamander's site: redirect it or drop it
problem: The legacy checkver plug-in still points at Open Salamander's (Altap's) site and is off in plugins.cfg. 072 recorded that winget handles updates for catalogue installs but nothing tells users who downloaded the installer from the website; the choice between the two ways out is a product decision, not code.
evidence: specs/072-winget-distribution/REMAINING-WORK.md, section P3. plugins.cfg line 17 'checkver=off' (at 7993914c). architecture/10-plugin-maintenance-outlook.md:90 (checkver points at Altap's servers; redirect to GitHub Releases API). Feature 123 (specs/FEATURE-HISTORY.md '- 123-new-version-check'): the core itself queries https://api.github.com/repos/tandemcommander/tandemcommander/releases/latest and notifies about a newer version. NEXT-WORK §6, P3 (L2044). Migrated from specs/NEXT-WORK.md §6 (at 7993914c).
expected: The maintainer has chosen; checkver is then either redirected (a feature) or removed from the tree and from architecture/10 (and plugins.cfg), with the update channel stated where users read it.
notes: The source gates the whole of section 6 on #426090; this decision itself touches no file under tools/winget/templates/ and could be unblocked by the maintainer. Its premise changed after the source entry was written: feature 123 already covers website downloads. The same entry is RW072 P3 and is listed in NW §B 'Release and catalogue housekeeping' - deduplicate on import. The recommendation below is the migrating agent's, from these facts; the source made none.
question: Should the checkver plug-in be pointed at the GitHub Releases API, or dropped, with winget and the program's own new-version notification (feature 123) declared the update channel?
options:
- A — point checkver at the GitHub Releases API (architecture/10 lists it under 'maintain with modernisation').
- B — drop checkver (it is off in plugins.cfg anyway); updates come through winget for catalogue installs and through the core's notification of feature 123 for everyone else; say so on the website.
recommendation: B — feature 123 already checks GitHub Releases from the core, so a second checker would duplicate it and add a network claim to PRIVACY.md if ever enabled.

title: Accented archive edits and long archive paths: rows the probes could not drive
problem: Features 096 (an edited archive member with a non-ASCII name is packed back) and 097 (archives with paths over 259 bytes refused instead of cut, later widened by 160) left rows the hidden-desktop probes could not drive: 096 - the RAR external packer with an accented name, a critical shutdown with an edited accented file, an accented %TEMP%; 097 - a real mouse drag.
evidence: specs/096-archive-edit-accented/fix-log.md ~line 51 'Not driven: the RAR external packer with an accented name; a critical shutdown with an edited accented file; an accented %TEMP%'. specs/097-archive-long-path/fix-log.md 'Not driven' and NEXT-WORK §5 L1536-1542 ('a real mouse drag was not driven'); drop/paste into such an archive was widened by feature 160 (NW §A.12). NEXT-WORK §5 L1929-1934. These rows are not in NW §B's person-step lists. Migrated from specs/NEXT-WORK.md §5 (at 7993914c).
expected: Each step below done once on a Release or Debug build and its result recorded; a failure becomes an item of its own.
notes: Check specs/096-archive-edit-accented/quickstart.md and specs/160-*/quickstart.md first - a step may already be written there. The 096 rows need WinRAR installed and configured as the external packer; the shutdown row needs a real sign-out or shutdown.
steps: (096) WinRAR configured as the external packer: F4 on a member with an accented name (e.g. `čšž.txt`) in a .rar archive, change and save, leave the archive -> the Archive Update question appears and the archive holds the edit.
(096) An F4 edit of an accented member pending (not packed back yet), then a real sign-out or shutdown -> no hang or loop; the temporary copy is kept, not deleted.
(096) %TEMP% / %TMP% set to a folder with an accented name, program restarted: F4 edit of an archive member, save, leave -> packed back.
(097, 160) A real mouse drag of a file from a panel onto a ZIP archive whose full path is longer than 259 bytes -> packed into that archive (no cut path, no other archive touched).

title: Two @GMT snapshot folders joined by a junction could hide a folder alias
reason: reasoned in feature 107's re-check, not reproducible without snapshots (agent sessions have no admin rights to create them)
problem: Feature 107 decides by folder identity whether a copy or move goes into the folder itself, and gives a path a snapshot tag (an @GMT- component, or a HarddiskVolumeShadowCopyN component of the final path) so that a live folder and its snapshot are not one. Two differently named @GMT folders joined by a junction could give the two sides different tags - a missed alias. Before 107 a move into itself through an alias deleted empty subfolders or moved the whole content one level down (nothing lost, the tree gone). Recorded with it: on FAT, two views reporting different times would miss an alias (reasoned).
evidence: specs/107-folder-alias-move/fix-log.md ~lines 232-235, 'Recorded (re-check NITs)'; CSalFileIdentity::SnapshotTag / SalSnapshotTagFromPath (fix-log ~line 28). NEXT-WORK §5 L1311-1312. Migrated from specs/NEXT-WORK.md §5 (at 7993914c).
expected: Either reproduced with real snapshots and refused like every other alias, or shown impossible.
approach: Needs a machine with volume shadow copies (admin) - ties in with NW §B 'Environment or hardware' (snapshots and FAT volumes, 107).
